tokyo_tofu_kawakaze.price_note: ⚠ THIS SHOP'S EXISTENCE IS NOT CONFIRMED AND THE RECORD IS HIDDEN IN THE APP. Tabelog has suspended the listing (掲載保留 — operating status unverifiable) and the shop's domain tofu-kawakaze.com no longer resolves. The menu below is recorded so it survives if the shop is confirmed trading; do not treat it as current. ⚠ WHY IT WOULD BE WORTH CONFIRMING: a tofu-and-yuba house is one of the few Japanese restaurant formats where a vegan has genuine choices, because the centre of the menu is soybean rather than fish or meat. But read it carefully rather than hopefully — this is an izakaya as well as a tofu specialist, most of the board is chicken, pork and fish, and the tofu dishes themselves are mostly dressed with dashi, soy or miso. 湯葉刺し and ざる豆腐 are the two that come closest to plant-only, and both are conventionally served with a soy dip. 浅草3-34-11; dinner only on weekdays, lunch at weekends, closed Mondays.

Most soba and udon shops leave a coeliac guessing at the flour; this one publishes it. THE SHOP STATES ITS OWN FLOUR: it blends 強力粉 and 中力粉 — strong and medium WHEAT flour — across four or five varieties, adjusted by the chef each year, with the dough aged three days and the noodles kneaded and cut by hand rather than by machine. That is an unusually precise description of a noodle, and every word of it is wheat. There is no ambiguity to chase here and no ratio to ask about — Sanuki udon is wheat by definition, and this shop is proud of exactly which wheats. tokyo_nepalico_shibuya_nepalic.price_note: ⚠ ONE OF THE BEST RECORDS IN THIS DATASET FOR BOTH DIETS, AND FOR REASONS THE SHOP ITSELF SUPPLIES. It marks vegetarian dishes with a V and prints the legend ※V＝Veg Menu — read that as VEGETARIAN rather than vegan, since it says nothing about dairy or ghee. More unusually, it STATES THE FLOUR IN TWO DISHES, which almost no restaurant does: its ポコラ is bound with ひよこ豆の粉 (CHICKPEA flour) and its チョタモリ is built on 米粉の生地 (a RICE-FLOUR base). Both are naturally gluten-free flours, named by the kitchen rather than inferred. Against that, its チャパティ is explicitly 全粒粉 — wholemeal WHEAT — and the モモ are wheat-wrapped dumplings. The structural point is that Nepali food is rice-and-lentil based: the ダルバート sets are rice, dal, tarkari, achar, sag and papad, and the shop gives free refills of dal and rice with them. Curry heat is adjustable 0 to 3 ピロ, and the shop notes the vegetable and chicken curries are effectively heat-0. Selected for Tabelog's アジア・エスニック TOKYO 百名店 2026.

This is a 煮込み shop — beef offal simmered for hours — and Japanese 煮込み is built on MISO and soy sauce. The miso is the part worth naming: Japanese miso is frequently 麦味噌, BARLEY, and barley is not on Japan's statutory allergen list, so no label anywhere will ever flag it. A coeliac has nothing published to work from here and would need to ask what the pot is seasoned with. Nothing on this board is vegan.

items.en: Simmered beef offal — the dish the shop is known for
items.note: Japanese 煮込み is offal simmered for hours in MISO and soy sauce. Two wheat-family routes in one bowl: the soy is wheat by default, and the miso is frequently 麦味噌 — barley — which Japanese allergen labelling does not cover. Beef offal rules out vegan.

The rice underneath is clean; what goes on it is not. A gyumeshi is beef simmered in soy, mirin and sugar, and at a 煮込み shop it is normally the same pot ladled over rice — so it carries whatever the nikomi carries.
